# The Tides Keep Their Promises

Forty-three years he had kept the light at Gannet Point, and the sea had never once spoken to him in a voice that wasn't wind or wave.

Eamon found the bottle on the Tuesday of the third week in October, when the fog rolled in thick enough to swallow the horizon whole. He'd gone down to the breakwater to check the mooring lines, boots slipping on barnacled stone, when something bright caught his eye half-submerged in the foam. A green bottle, its neck sealed with wax the color of dried blood. Inside, a rolled slip of paper.

He held it up against the grey sky. The glass was warm from the sun's earlier effort before the clouds sealed the world shut. He uncorked it slowly, the wax cracking with a sound like a knuckle popping, and pulled the paper free
